Patients with 5 or fewer metastatic sites at the time of diagnosis tend to have significantly better survival rates compared to those with more extensive metastasis. This is because existing sites of metastatic disease may be the primary locations where additional metastases originate, potentially impacting long-term outcomes.

In fact, our findings suggest that early detection and aggressive treatment of patients with a small number of metastatic lesions may be worth exploring as an approach to improving long-term survival rates. By addressing these initial sites of spread, healthcare providers can more effectively manage the disease, potentially leading to better patient outcomes.
